criteria.text: `pnpm typecheck` passes with `'senado'` added to the `Source` union in `src/types.ts` and `senadoId?: string` added to `Person`.

`src/collectors/senado.ts` exports a `Collector` (same signature `Person[] -> Promise<RawDoc[]>`) that returns `[]` when called with persons that all lack `senadoId` — no network call is made (assert via a spy/mock or by construction, not a live request, per the no-external-calls-in-tests constraint).
Every `RawDoc` produced by the collector has `source: 'senado'` and `tone === undefined`.

`src/collectors/index.ts` registers `senado` in `collectors` and includes it in `defaultSources`, so `pnpm ingest` with no arguments now also collects `senado` (default, not opt-in — justified in section 3: no observed rate limiting, unlike `gdelt`).

`src/query.ts`'s `SOURCES` array, the `rising` source check, and the `timeline` source check (lines 13, 46, 57) all include `'senado'`; a `GET .../rising?source=senado` or `.../timeline?source=senado` request is honored (not silently downgraded to `all`) — covered by `parseRisingQuery`/`parseTimelineQuery` assertions added to `test/server.test.ts`.

`test/fixture.ts` gains one `senado` doc, dated outside every window ( > 3100 days ago) any existing test opens, with vocabulary that does not appear in any other fixture doc; every existing test in the suite (`pnpm test`) still passes unmodified with no literal recomputed.

A test in `test/extract.test.ts` (or `test/store.test.ts`) asserts the new senado doc's person mention is picked up by `personsMentioned`/`insertDoc` with no `source === 'senado'` branch anywhere in `src/extract.ts` (i.e. the test would pass identically if the doc's `source` were swapped for `'rss'`).

`GET /api/people/:id/graph?source=senado` for a person with no senado docs in the fixture returns `{ nodes: [], links: [], signature: [] }`-shaped response with `stats.docs === 0`, not an error — covered by a `graph.test.ts` case.
`seed.json` has `senadoId: "5894"` on `flavio-bolsonaro` and `senadoId: "3830"` on `alcolumbre`, and no other entry.

README documents `senado` in the source list (line 3), the `pnpm ingest` default-sources line (line 9), the `source=` enum in every route that lists one (lines 33, 37, 45, 47, 49), the `senadoId` seed field (near line 75), and a short paragraph next to the `gdelt`/`gkg` paragraphs (near line 27) stating `senado` is on by default with the observed no-rate-limit rationale.

`public/design-5.html`'s `segSource` control includes a `senado` button; clicking it sets `state.source = 'senado'` and triggers `load()` — checkable by reading the `buildSeg('segSource', ...)` call, no automated UI test required (no existing UI test harness in this repo).
